about: Who is covering Storm Charles (Lisbon, 10 to 12 November 2026): press articles and live blogs (`articles`), the official channels (`official`) and what can be read of social platforms without a login (`social`). Every article: outlet, URL, title, the time the page itself says it was published (UTC), the by-line as the page prints it, the time we read it, and the sha256 of our capture (the capture is kept outside git). All of it is evidence: reported by others. Not a warning service: follow IPMA and ANEPC.
rules: People appear only as a by-line printed on a public article or as a body's official account: a name, nothing else. No contact details, no profiles, no private individuals.
Posts by individuals on social platforms are counted, never listed.
Titles are quoted as short excerpts with a link; no article text is kept here.
Times are UTC (Lisbon is on UTC in November). A time the page gives without an offset is taken as Lisbon time and says so in `published_from`.
how: research/media/tools/harvest.mjs (feeds.json, the incident's cited URLs) -> social.mjs -> rank.mjs. See README.md for the limits.
limits: Only outlets whose public feed, news sitemap or cited page answered a plain bot are here: SIC Notícias, Jornal de Notícias, TSF, Renascença, The Guardian and AP refused (403), so their absence says nothing about their coverage.
Where a page refused but its feed or sitemap listed it (Expresso, The Portugal News, Bloomberg), the title and time are the feed's and the by-line was not read.
A live blog has one publication time; the minute of each entry inside it is not in this file.
Feeds scroll: items older than a feed's window at the first read (23:45 UTC, 10 November) are missing unless cited elsewhere in the incident.

counts.wire_share_note: items with the agency's (Lusa's) by-line, over items whose by-line we read

removed.why: no automated reading: its terms forbid automated and AI uses of its content (terms read 2026-11-11T02:15Z by incident.weatherwatch@, research/weather-sites/terms.json). We make no requests to it; we keep its address and our own one-line description only. Whether a person asks it for permission is Dinis's decision. Its items (titles and times from its public feed, read before 02:15) were removed from this file.

official.about: The official channels on the storm: the bodies that decide or warn, and the organiser. Read from data/decisions/sources.json (kept by incident.researcher@), which holds what each contains and how a machine reads it; `status` and `read` are that file's. Official accounts on X, Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn cannot be read without a login. Organisations' accounts that can be read are under `social.accounts`.
